A1.justification: Both readable 12-page PDFs describe the same PT2-LLM work and support comparison of all supplied text, equations, figures, tables, and references. Neither contains appendices or an embedded supplement; both reference supplementary material that is not supplied.

before.justification: v1 reports original PT2-LLM benchmark evaluations, component and calibration ablations, compression measurements, and inference throughput results in Tables 1–3 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, compression measurements, and throughput results reported in v1.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same asymmetric ternary initialization, Iterative Ternary Fitting, Activation-aware Grid Alignment, and Structural Similarity-based Reordering procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions retain WikiText2/C4 perplexity evaluation, the same seven zero-shot QA benchmarks, PTB in the calibration ablation, and the same LLaMA and Qwen3 coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains FP16, AWQ, GPTQ, QuIP, Slim-LLM, and PB-LLM with identical comparator participation. The reordering, compression, and throughput comparisons also retain their respective comparator sets.

E3.justification: The settings remain identical, including 128 calibration samples of 2048 tokens, block size 128, evaluation metrics, model sizes, calibration ablation settings, and inference sequence lengths.

E4.justification: Table 2 retains the same ITF/AGA, reordering, calibration-size, and calibration-dataset ablations. Figure 3 and the compression and inference analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The same point-estimate reporting is retained.

E6.justification: All reported result entries and plotted findings match. For example, PT2-LLM on LLaMA-7B retains 11.39 WikiText2 perplexity and 45.07% average QA accuracy in Table 1, and 1.88 GB model size and 32-minute compression time in Table 3.

T1.justification: Equations 1–16 and their accompanying mathematical reasoning are unchanged, including the ternary optimization objectives, closed-form parameter updates, and permutation formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free ternarization, ATQ and SSR, competitive accuracy, reduced memory, and faster inference.

C2.justification: Both retain the same mechanism explanations and qualifications, including calibration overfitting when updating T during AGA, the rationale for SSR, and interpretations of calibration and efficiency results.

D1.justification: Implementation and access information are unchanged: PyTorch/Huggingface, a single NVIDIA A800-80GB GPU, calibration and block settings, llama.cpp inference, and the same prospective code/model availability statement.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, reference entries, and positioning within post-training ternarization are identical.

P1.justification: v2 adds the header 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026' and updates the arXiv version/date marking. The paper's prose, terminology, headings, and section order are unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the publication header throughout and slightly changes first-page spacing and the margin stamp. Figures 1–4, Tables 1–3, and Algorithm 1 retain their displays, captions, and organization.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, evidence, explanations, and reproducibility information are unchanged. The publication header, updated version/date marking, and small spacing adjustments do not materially improve or impair the paper's overall quality.
